processing: Withered and dried with no firing or rolling, with temperature-controlled modern handling.
harvest_season: Spring is usual for the class. The county standard picks only a single bud or one bud with one leaf.
appearance_dry: Fine buds and young leaf, as the picking standard requires, with downy silver-green tones.
appearance_wet: Tender single buds and bud-with-leaf sets, soft and pale green.
taste_profile: Its official description is a bright yellow liquor, a mellow sweet taste, a floral scent and a long finish.
vintage_note: Mostly sold as branded recent harvests in a local range such as the Feng Hua Xue Yue series. Little is documented about an aged market, so judge older stock with care.
description:
Sangzhi is a mountain county in the Wuling range near Zhangjiajie in north-west Hunan, better known for scenery than for white tea. Over the past decade it has built up a white tea industry, and it now has its own protected name.

The tea follows the white tea pattern of withering and drying, with no firing or rolling, helped by modern temperature control. The county standard asks for a single bud or one bud and a leaf, so the base material is young.

The local shorthand for the cup is yellow and bright, mellow and sweet, with a hint of flower and a long finish. It reads as a soft, approachable white.

The industry is young and heavily organised around one public brand, so look for a named maker and a harvest year.
history:
Sangzhi's white tea is a recent, deliberately built industry. County gardens went from around 20,000 mu in 2012 to around 79,000 mu by 2021, brand building began in 2016, and Sangzhi Bai Cha was named one of Hunan's five supported regional brands in 2018.

It gained a national geographic indication certification mark in 2019. The first Sangzhi white tea culture festival took place in May 2021. Local publicity also claims a tradition of over 700 years, brought from Yunnan by Bai people, and a Ming tribute tea; treat these as promotional stories.
